Type: Remote, Non-Exclusive Contractor Role

Location: Remote



About the Role



We are hiring a reliable Coverage Virtual Assistant to provide dependable on-call support during assigned coverage hours.



This is a request-based role. You are not expected to stay continuously busy or actively monitor systems when there is nothing requiring your attention.



Instead, you are expected to remain reachable and responsive during your assigned shift and respond promptly when a request comes in.



When there are no active requests, you are free to work on other jobs, clients, or projects, provided that your outside work does not interfere with your ability to respond when needed.



This role is best suited for someone who is comfortable handling light creative, technical, and administrative tasks, including Canva editing, AI image editing, and basic GoHighLevel updates.



How the Role Works



During your assigned coverage hours, you will:



Be reachable and available.

Respond promptly when a request comes in.

Handle straightforward creative, technical, or administrative requests.

Make simple Canva edits when needed.

Create or edit images using AI tools.

Complete basic GoHighLevel updates.

Escalate or assign more complex requests to the correct person.

Follow through until the request is completed or clearly handed off.

Provide a brief handoff at the end of your shift if anything remains open.



When there is no request requiring your attention, you may work on other flexible projects.



Your outside work must not prevent you from responding promptly when needed.



Responsibilities



You may be asked to:



Make simple edits in Canva, including graphics, presentations, social media posts, PDFs, and basic layouts.

Make light updates inside GoHighLevel (GHL).

Make basic adjustments to simple workflows, settings, or other straightforward GHL items when instructed.

Make small website or landing-page updates.

Update documents, graphics, presentations, or other digital assets.

Complete simple administrative or operational tasks.

Locate information, files, images, or digital assets.

Respond to incoming team requests during your shift.

Route more complicated requests to the appropriate team member or specialist.

Escalate urgent matters quickly.

Follow up on specific outstanding tasks when asked.

Record important updates for the next person.

Make sure open requests are properly handed off before your shift ends.



You will not be responsible for constantly checking calendars or continuously monitoring systems throughout the day.



Responsiveness Standard



Responsiveness is the most important requirement for this role.



You do not need to spend your entire shift actively watching communication channels.



However, when a request is sent during your assigned coverage hours, you should be reachable, acknowledge it promptly, and begin handling or routing it without unnecessary delay.



If you are able to complete the request yourself, you should do so.



If the request is outside your experience or requires more advanced work, you should escalate it instead of guessing.



If another job or project regularly prevents you from responding when needed, this role will not be a good fit.



What You Are Not Expected to Do



You are not expected to:



Continuously monitor systems all day.

Constantly check calendars.

Create unnecessary work when there are no requests.

Personally complete every complex technical project.

Handle advanced GoHighLevel development.

Guess when you are unsure how to complete something.

Stay focused exclusively on our business during quiet periods.



This role is intentionally designed to allow you to work on other flexible projects while remaining available when our team needs assistance.



When a Request Comes In



The normal process is:



Request Received → Acknowledge → Handle if Appropriate → Escalate or Assign if Needed → Confirm Status → Handoff if Still Open



Straightforward requests should be completed when possible.



More complex work will normally be handled by the primary team member or specialist responsible for that area.



Shift Handoff



If something remains open when your shift ends, provide a short handoff explaining:



What was requested

What has already been done

What is still pending

Whether anything is urgent

Who should handle the next step



The next Coverage VA or team member should be able to continue the request without having to start over.



What We Are Looking For



We want someone who is:



Reliable

Highly responsive

Organized

Comfortable working independently

Able to follow instructions carefully

Comfortable using Canva

Comfortable with AI image generation and image editing

Familiar with GoHighLevel, or able to confidently handle basic GHL tasks

Comfortable making simple website, page, funnel, and digital asset updates

Able to recognize urgency

Comfortable escalating instead of guessing

A strong written communicator

Comfortable learning new software and tools

Comfortable using Google Workspace, messaging platforms, Canva, AI tools, GoHighLevel, and other common business software



You do not need to be an expert in every platform.



We care more about your ability to follow instructions, learn quickly, respond reliably, and know when to ask for help or escalate a request.



Success in This Role



You are succeeding when:



You are available during your assigned coverage hours.

Requests are acknowledged promptly.

Straightforward tasks are handled efficiently.

Canva edits are completed accurately.

AI image requests are completed according to instructions.

Basic GoHighLevel updates are handled correctly.

Urgent matters are escalated quickly.

Complex requests reach the correct person.

Nothing important is forgotten during handoffs.

You remain dependable while still having the flexibility to work on other projects during quiet periods.

title: UX App designer and human psychology expert
description:
UX Designer & Behavioral Psychology Consultant (Contract, Remote)





We built an app that works, but people keep telling us it's confusing. We need someone who can actually explain why, and then help us fix it.



This is a contract role for someone who lives at the intersection of UX design and human psychology. We're not looking for someone to just redesign screens. We want someone who can look at how people actually behave when they use our app, figure out where the friction and confusion is really coming from, and give us clear, practical recommendations we can act on.



What you'll be doing



You'll dig into our current app and map out where users get stuck, confused, or drop off. That means reviewing our flows, talking to us about user behavior patterns, and possibly reviewing session recordings or analytics if we have them. From there, you'll put together a set of recommendations grounded in actual behavioral principles, not just design trends. Cognitive load, decision fatigue, mental models, all of that. We want to understand not just what to change, but why it's confusing in the first place.



Depending on scope, this could extend into redesigning specific flows or screens once we've agreed on the direction.



What we're looking for



Someone with real UX design experience, ideally with apps rather than just websites. Beyond that, we need someone who genuinely understands psychology as it applies to product design. That might mean a background in cognitive or behavioral psychology, UX research with a psychology lean, or just years of experience applying that thinking to real products. We'd rather see strong reasoning and a track record than a specific degree.



You should be comfortable auditing an existing product critically and telling us hard truths if that's what the data shows. We want someone who can back up their recommendations with actual reasoning, not just opinions on what looks nice.



Good to have



Experience with fintech or e-commerce apps, familiarity with tools like Figma, Maze, or Hotjar, and any past work where you can point to a measurable improvement after your recommendations were implemented.



Details



This is a remote, contract-based engagement. Scope and timeline will be discussed based on what the audit uncovers, this could be a one-time deep review or an ongoing relationship if it's a good fit. Send us your portfolio along with a short note on how you'd approach a project like this.

Responsibilities

Building, configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting technical systems across multiple businesses, communities, creators, campaigns, and projects.

Creating, editing, and correcting videos when needed, including presentation videos, intros, effects, animations, transitions, audio, screen recordings, and basic production work.

Preparing and testing technical systems and assets for launches, campaigns, webinars, communities, creators, presentations, and other initiatives.

Maintaining organized accounts, access, naming conventions, documentation, templates, and basic SOPs.

How We Work



Take ownership of your work through completion. Communicate progress without waiting to be asked, raise meaningful issues early, test your own work, and proactively identify and address problems rather than waiting for every task to be assigned.



Independent thinking and resourcefulness are essential. When you encounter something you do not know, use AI extensively to research, diagnose, and solve the problem. Also use documentation, tutorials, knowledge bases, internet research, community resources, and software-company support. If specialized help is ultimately required, identify the right resource while continuing to own the issue through resolution.



When disagreeing, do it productively. Proactively investigate before challenging, while escalating immediately if even reasonable investigation could create material harm or serious risk. Otherwise, make reasonable progress and validate concerns with facts before raising them. When raising a concern, bring what you learned and, whenever possible, a recommended solution, practical options, or clear next step.



Be settled, connected, and ready before meetings. Follow through on commitments, communicate when something is delayed or blocked, and correct mistakes quickly when they happen.



Think from the user's perspective. Technical correctness matters, but so do clarity, usability, consistency, and the complete experience of the person using what you build.



We do not expect perfection or that you will know everything. We do expect independent problem-solving, proactive action, communication, accountability, and follow-through.



What We're Looking For



You should have:



Strong written English and communication skills.

Reliable internet and the ability to work consistently and independently.

Strong attention to detail, organization, and technical aptitude.

The ability to encounter unfamiliar technical problems and independently work toward solutions.

A genuine passion for technology and especially AI.

A habit of staying current with new AI tools, capabilities, and trends, particularly how AI is changing technology, marketing, and business.

Natural curiosity about new tools and the ability to identify practical ways they can improve systems, automation, marketing, content, and user experience.



Experience with some of the following is helpful, but you do not need to know everything:



GoHighLevel, Votel, WordPress, websites and funnels, CRM systems, forms and calendars,
 configuration, workflows, custom fields, APIs, webhooks, Zapier, Make, domains and DNS, integrations, communities, marketing automation, CapCut, Descript, DaVinci Resolve, Canva, Adobe Premiere, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and similar platforms.



Do not skip applying because you do not check every box. We would rather hire someone capable, dependable, curious, and resourceful who knows how to figure things out than someone who claims to know everything.



What Success Looks Like



When you are assigned something, you think beyond the individual task and consider the complete system and user experience.



If you build a page, for example, you make sure it is in the correct account, contains the right content, has working links, connects to the correct form or calendar, sends information where it should go, works on desktop and mobile, makes sense to the user, and has been tested before you call it complete.



When you encounter something unfamiliar, you research it, use AI and available support resources, test potential solutions, and keep moving. You look ahead for problems and opportunities rather than waiting for someone else to identify every next step.



Working Relationship



This is intended to be a long-term working relationship for the right person. We hire on a month-to-month basis, with the expectation that the first month gives both parties an opportunity to establish a strong working rhythm and determine whether continuing together makes sense.



We are looking for someone who wants to become a reliable, long-term part of the team, not someone looking for a short-term project or a few days of work.



This is a freelance/independent contractor role. Continued work depends on performance, reliability, communication, business needs, and mutual fit.



To Apply



Please include:



A short introduction about yourself.

Your relevant technical and systems experience.

Your experience with GoHighLevel or similar platforms.

Examples of websites, funnels, automations, integrations, or other systems you have personally built or managed.

Your video editing and production experience, if any.

The AI tools you currently use and how you use them to solve technical problems.

An example of a new AI tool, capability, or trend you have recently explored and why you found it useful.

Your availability, timezone, and internet speed.

Why you are interested in a long-term role like this.



Scenario: You are asked to implement something and initially believe there may be a technical problem with the requested approach. It does not appear to create an immediate serious risk. Walk us through what you would do before raising the concern, and how you would communicate it if your investigation confirms there is a better approach.



Please start your application with the words:



IT READY

title: Dispute & Chargeback Manager + Customer Support VA Wanted for Fast-Growing eCommerce Company
description:
Hey there,



We’re looking for an experienced Dispute & Chargeback Manager / Customer Support VA to join our eCommerce business long-term.



This is an important role because you will be responsible for protecting revenue, making sure disputes are handled correctly and on time, and communicating professionally with customers.



We are specifically looking for someone who has real hands-on experience with disputes and chargebacks. We are not looking for someone who has only worked in general customer support or has basic knowledge from watching tutorials.



Because dispute volume changes from week to week, you will also handle regular customer support 6 days per week when there are fewer disputes.



Your responsibilities



You will be responsible for:



- Monitoring disputes and chargebacks and making sure no deadline is ever missed

- Collecting all relevant dispute evidence

- Preparing and submitting strong, organized dispute responses

- Fighting chargebacks through platforms such as Shopify Payments, PayPal, and Stripe for the following payment methods: paypal, creditcard and Klarna

- Communicating with customers professionally and trying to resolve disputes before they escalate

- Persuading customers to voluntarily close disputes when appropriate

- Keeping our dispute tracking sheet completely up to date

- Handling normal customer-support tickets when dispute workload is lower

- Following our customer-support and refund SOPs carefully

- Knowing when to solve a case yourself and when something should be escalated



What we are looking for



You should:



- Have previous hands-on eCommerce dispute/chargeback experience

- Understand different dispute reasons such as item not received, fraudulent transaction, product not as described, refund/cancellation disputes, etc.

- Have experience with Shopify Payments/Stripe and PayPal

- Be highly organized and good at managing deadlines

- Have excellent attention to detail

- Write clear and professional English

- Be comfortable dealing with angry or difficult customers

- Be able to follow detailed SOPs without constantly needing reminders

- Be available for customer support 6 days per week

- Take responsibility for mistakes instead of hiding them

- Be able to work independently and think logically



Important



Please do not apply if your only experience is answering customer-support
s.



We will ask detailed questions about your previous dispute-management experience, and shortlisted applicants will receive a practical test involving realistic dispute and customer-support cases.



We care much more about what you can actually do than how good your application sounds.



When applying, answer these questions



1. How many disputes/chargebacks did you personally handle per month in your previous role?

2. Which platforms did you personally use to submit disputes?

3. Explain what evidence you would collect for an Item Not Received chargeback when tracking shows the order was delivered.

4. Tell us about one dispute you lost and why you think you lost it.

5. How did you make sure you never missed dispute deadlines?

6. Have you handled eCommerce customer support as well? Which helpdesk/platform did you use?

7. Are you available to work/check customer support 6 days per week?

8. What hourly rate are you looking for for this role?



We are looking for someone who can become a reliable long-term member of the company, take ownership of this department and eventually require very little supervision.



If you genuinely have strong dispute-management experience, we would love to hear from you.

* Designing high-quality Instagram carousels and educational graphics

* Editing short-form video and Reels

* Adding dynamic captions, typography, transitions, graphics and visual storytelling

* Repurposing longer videos into polished social content

* Creating branded templates and visual assets

Ideal candidate

* Your hourly rate

title: Order Fulfillment & Customer Support VA — Vinted resale | Part-Time | $100–200/mo
description:
Order Fulfillment & Customer Support VA—Vinted resale



To apply, start your message with the word BAGUETTE. Messages without it are ignored.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

Part-time to start (~15–20h/week). Likely full-time within a few months, at a higher rate, as the business grows.

- Log incoming supplier parcels into our warehouse system: tracking number, contents, and SKU.

- Process outgoing orders: download shipping labels from our dashboard (DOTB) and create the shipment requests in the warehouse system.

- Answer buyer messages on Vinted that our auto-responder escalates—using ready-made reply templates that you adapt.

- Handle disputes and returns (item not received, not as described) by following a written procedure; escalate the tricky ones to me.

- Keep everything logged in a Google Sheet.

- Later: a few simple, low-risk steps of new shop setup.



ABOUT THE BUSINESS

I buy fashion items and resell them on Vinted (a French second-hand marketplace) across several shops, with a fulfillment warehouse in Europe. I need a reliable assistant to run daily operations so I can focus on growth.



YOU NEED

- Good written English—we work in English. Buyer replies are in French, but you write them with a ChatGPT prompt I give you (no French skills required; you just need to check the output makes sense).

- Reliable internet, quiet setup; available in a daily window overlapping European afternoon (~1–7pm Paris time).

- Detail-oriented; comfortable with Google Sheets, web dashboards, and using ChatGPT.

- Calm and polite with unhappy customers; good judgment on when to escalate.

- Bonus: experience with Vinted, Depop, Poshmark, or e-commerce support.



PAY

$100–200/month part-time (~15–20h/week) to start, reviewed after 1 month. Moves to full-time at a higher rate as volume grows.

title: Trucking Contract Procurement & Dispatch Assistant — 4-Week Contract
description:
Weekend Pro Logistics LLC is seeking a Virtual Assistant for an initial 4-week contract focused on finding and securing local trucking opportunities in Florida.

Our immediate focus is:

Southwest Florida: Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Lee County and surrounding areas

Jacksonville: Jacksonville and surrounding areas

We are primarily seeking:

Box-truck delivery contracts

Dump-truck/aggregate hauling contracts

Dedicated local routes

Final-mile delivery opportunities

Construction/material hauling

Broker and subcontractor opportunities

Responsibilities

Research and contact companies that contract with trucking companies, identify opportunities that fit our equipment strategy, make outbound calls/emails, complete carrier/vendor applications, follow up consistently, maintain a simple opportunity tracker, and assist with dispatch/load research when needed.

This is not simply a lead-generation position. The objective is to move qualified opportunities from research through application/onboarding toward an actual contract or recurring work opportunity.

4-Week Performance Milestones

Week 1: Build and contact a qualified prospect list and identify at least 3 serious opportunities.

Week 2: Complete applications/onboarding and move qualified prospects into active discussions.

Week 3: Follow up, obtain rates/requirements and work toward securing contracts.

Week 4: Close qualified opportunities and prepare a handoff/report of the active pipeline.

Compensation

Base contract: $5–$7 USD/hour, up to 20 hours per week for 4 weeks.

Performance bonuses are based on contracts secured

# Video Editor / Short Form Content (Full Time)



**Type:** Full time

**Salary:** $600/month retainer

**Hours:** Flexible, built around output rather than a clock. We need overlap with MST Colorado USA or feedback and handoffs.





I need someone who turns raw footage into content that actually gets watched. Long form recordings, talking head clips, screen recordings, phone footage, whatever I send you. You cut it, caption it, and make it ready to post.



Most of the work is short form. Reels, TikToks, Shorts, ad creative. Some weeks it will be five clips. Some weeks it will be twenty. You need to be able to move fast without the quality dropping off.  Taking long form youtueb videos and clipping. adding captions, getting ready for ads.  



Speed and efficienty and effective is the GOAL



This is not a job where I send you a storyboard. I send you a raw file and a rough idea, and you come back with something I can post.



What you will actually be doing



- Cutting long form recordings into short clips that stand on their own

- Captions, hooks, pacing, b roll, sound design, light motion graphics

- Ad creative for Meta. Multiple versions of the same concept for testing

- Thumbnails and cover frames

- Keeping files organized so nothing gets lost or re-edited twice

- Occasionally shooting simple screen recordings or assembling from stock



Tools



Premiere Pro, CapCut, DaVinci, Final Cut, whatever you are fastest in. I care about the output, not the software. After Effects is a plus.  OPUS CLAUDE



YOU NEED TO BE USING AI OR YOU WILL BE LET GO IMMEDIATELY 



You should also be comfortable with the AI tools that speed editing up. Auto captioning, transcription, clip finding, upscaling, voice cleanup. If you are still cutting captions by hand, you are too slow for this.



AI is non-negotiable



This is the most important part of the posting, so read it twice.



Editing today does not look like editing five years ago. Auto captions, AI cut detection, transcript based editing, AI upscaling, voice cleanup, AI b-roll and stock search, even rough assembly, all of it should be part of how you work. We use tools like Claude and Opus for scripting, planning, and content decisions, so being comfortable working alongside AI tools day to day matters, not just inside your editing software. If you are still doing everything by hand the slow way, you will not keep up with the pace we need.



Because AI is doing a lot of the heavy lifting now, I expect real output. Not fewer hours for the same result, more finished content in less time. That is the trade. You use the tools, you move faster, and the volume reflects it.



Tell me exactly which AI tools you use and what each one does for you in your process. If your answer is vague or you skip this part, I will assume you are not actually using AI and this is not a fit.



Who this works for



- You have a real eye for pacing and hooks, not just technical editing skill

- You watch short form content enough to know what is working right now

- You hit deadlines without being chased

- You take feedback without getting precious about the work

- You can hold a consistent style across dozens of pieces



Who this does not work for



- You need every cut spelled out for you

- You are slow but "thorough"

- You disappear for two days when you hit a problem

- You only do one style and cannot adapt



How to apply



Do not send a generic application. I will skip it.



Send me:



1. Three examples of short form work you edited. Links, not descriptions.

2. One long form video you cut down, plus the clips that came out of it if you have them.

3. What you edit in, and roughly how long a 60 second clip takes you start to finish using your current AI-assisted workflow.

4. Which AI tools you use at each stage of editing (captions, cutting, cleanup, etc.) and what each one does for you.

5. Your realistic weekly output using that workflow. How many finished short clips can you turn around per week at a quality you are proud of.

6. Start your message with the word ORANGE so I know you read this all the way through.



If you also shoot, write hooks, or handle posting and scheduling, mention it. It changes what this role can grow into.

title: Executive & Operations Assistant to Founder
description:
Executive & Operations Assistant to Founder



Remote – Philippines | Part-Time Initially | Long-Term Opportunity



About Northwest Floors



Northwest Floors is an established flooring business based in Cheshire, UK. We supply and install LVT, carpets, laminate, engineered wood and other flooring products for residential and commercial customers.



We are a growing business with a showroom, fitting teams, suppliers and a busy schedule of installations.



I’m the owner of the business and I’m looking for an exceptional Executive & Operations Assistant who can become my right-hand person.



This is much more than a traditional Virtual Assistant position.



I’m looking for somebody who can gradually help me run and coordinate the day-to-day operation of the business, while also supporting me personally as the owner.



My goal is to spend more of my time on sales, customers, relationships, marketing and growing Northwest Floors — and less time chasing people, coordinating jobs, answering routine
s, checking orders and remembering hundreds of small things.



Your job will be to help make that happen.



⸻



The Person I’m Looking For



The most important qualities I’m looking for are:



Ownership, initiative, organisation and communication.



I don’t want somebody who waits all day to be given tasks.



I want somebody who notices things.



If a fitter hasn’t confirmed tomorrow’s job, you notice.



If a supplier hasn’t confirmed a delivery, you chase it.



If a customer is waiting for an update, you make sure they receive one.



If someone says they’ll send something tomorrow, you remember tomorrow so I don’t have to.



If you spot something that could become a problem next week, you raise it before it becomes a problem.



Ultimately, I want somebody who starts to think:



“What can I take care of so Alex doesn’t need to?”



⸻



Your Responsibilities



The position will develop as you learn the business and gain my trust.



Initially, your responsibilities will include:



Executive Assistance



* Managing and organising my
 inbox

* Drafting and responding to
s on my behalf

* Identifying
s that genuinely require my attention

* Managing my business and personal calendar

* Organising appointments and meetings

* Helping protect my time and avoid unnecessary interruptions

* Turning my WhatsApp messages and voice notes into organised tasks

* Keeping track of things I’ve said I’ll do

* Chasing people on my behalf

* Helping with occasional personal administration, appointments, bookings and research

* Producing concise daily updates so I know what genuinely needs my attention



The objective is for you to gradually become an external brain for me, making sure things don’t get forgotten.



⸻



Customer Communication



You will become an important point of contact for our customers.



This will include:



* Answering routine customer
s

* Communicating with customers through
, telephone and WhatsApp

* Confirming appointments and installation dates

* Keeping customers informed about their upcoming flooring installation

* Informing customers of fitter arrival times

* Following up outstanding quotations

* Chasing deposits where appropriate

* Gathering information required before installations

* Helping resolve routine questions

* Following up after installations

* Coordinating snagging or outstanding work

* Helping ensure final balances are collected



You must be confident communicating in English and comfortable speaking directly with UK customers.



Customer service is extremely important to us, so communication should always be professional, friendly and proactive.



⸻



Managing Flooring Projects



A major part of this position will eventually be taking ownership of projects after the sale has been made and the customer has paid their deposit.



I enjoy meeting customers, helping them choose their flooring and making the sale.



What I want to move away from is having to personally manage every detail that happens afterwards.



Once a project is handed over, you will help coordinate the journey through to completion.



This will include:



* Checking the job information is complete

* Confirming fitting dates

* Liaising with fitters

* Liaising with Josh in our showroom

* Checking materials have been ordered

* Confirming supplier deliveries

* Making sure materials have arrived before they’re required

* Checking preparation requirements

* Ensuring fitters have the information they need

* Keeping the customer informed

* Coordinating access and other trades where required

* Monitoring jobs while they are taking place

* Recording changes or additional work

* Collecting completion information

* Collecting photographs from our fitters for our records and social media

* Coordinating snagging or return visits

* Making sure completed jobs are invoiced

* Following up outstanding balances



I don’t expect you to understand all of this immediately.



We will teach you.



Over time, however, I want you to understand our processes well enough to take genuine ownership of them.



⸻



Working With Our Team & Fitters



You’ll act as an important link between me, Josh, our fitters, customers and suppliers.



Part of your job is making sure information gets to the right person and that agreed actions actually happen.



For example, if Josh needs to order flooring for an upcoming installation, you may not necessarily place that particular order yourself.



However, you may be responsible for making sure it has been ordered, checking the supplier has acknowledged it and confirming it will arrive in time.



The same applies to our fitters.



You will help confirm their schedules, make sure they have job information and follow up when information is outstanding.



The aim is that I no longer need to be the person remembering and chasing everything.



⸻



Stock Control & Forward Planning



You will also help manage our regularly used stock and installation materials.



I don’t simply want someone who counts stock.



I want somebody who looks ahead.



You will regularly review our confirmed jobs for approximately the next 4–6 weeks and make sure we are likely to have enough materials available.



This will include monitoring items such as:



* Smoothing compounds

* Primers

* Flooring adhesives

* DPM products

* Underlays

* Plywood

* Flooring accessories

* Other regularly used installation materials



You will:



* Carry out regular stock checks

* Maintain accurate stock records

* Understand what stock has already been allocated to specific jobs

* Look at upcoming jobs and estimate likely requirements

* Check supplier lead times

* Identify potential shortages early

* Liaise with Josh and our fitters about requirements

* Recommend or arrange replenishment

* Flag unusual stock usage or discrepancies

* Help prevent unnecessary over-ordering

* Produce a simple forward stock forecast



The objective is:



We should know what we’re going to need before we need it.



I don’t want us discovering on the morning of an installation that we’ve run out of an important product.



⸻



Learning About Flooring



You do not need previous flooring experience to apply.



However, you must genuinely want to learn about the industry.



I don’t want somebody who is still saying “I don’t really understand flooring” a year after joining us.



We will dedicate a minimum of one paid hour every week specifically to flooring education and product knowledge.



This could include learning about:



* LVT

* Carpet

* Laminate

* Engineered wood

* Different installation methods

* Subfloors

* Moisture

* Smoothing compounds

* DPMs

* Plywood preparation

* Adhesives

* Underlays

* Measuring and wastage

* Common installation problems

* Our major manufacturers and product ranges



I can also arrange for you to speak directly with our suppliers and manufacturers and participate in product training so that you can learn from people within the industry.



You will be encouraged to ask questions.



The purpose isn’t to turn you into a flooring installer.



It’s to give you enough understanding that when a customer, fitter or supplier discusses a flooring issue, you understand what they’re talking about.



The more you learn, the more decisions you’ll eventually be able to make independently.



⸻



Administration & Financial Organisation



As the position develops, you will also help us keep our administration organised.



This may include:



* Matching supplier invoices against orders

* Checking purchase information

* Assisting with QuickBooks administration

* Monitoring outstanding customer balances

* Checking deposits have been received

* Maintaining job records

* Keeping CRM information accurate

* Checking paperwork is complete

* Helping with basic reporting



You don’t need to be an accountant.



The important thing is being accurate, organised and comfortable working with numbers and systems.



⸻



How I Want Problems Handled



Things inevitably go wrong in a flooring business.



Deliveries get delayed.



Customers change dates.



Fitters become unavailable.



Unexpected preparation is discovered.



I don’t expect you to magically solve everything.



But I also don’t want every problem simply forwarded to me with:



“Alex, what should I do?”



I want you to investigate first.



Ideally, you come to me with:



“This has happened. I’ve looked into it. We have option A or option B. I recommend option B because of X. Are you happy for me to proceed?”



As your knowledge and experience grow, there will be more situations where you won’t need to ask me at all.



That’s how I want this position to develop.



⸻



Communication With Me



I don’t want 30 interruptions every day.



Part of your job will be understanding what genuinely requires my attention.



I’d like us to develop a simple system where I receive a concise update containing things such as:



HANDLED



Things you’ve dealt with that I don’t need to worry about.



WAITING



Things we’re waiting for somebody else to provide.



NEEDS ALEX



Decisions or actions that genuinely require me.



HEADS-UP



Something you’ve spotted that could become an issue.



The ultimate goal is for me to be able to look at one short update and understand what is happening across the business.



⸻



What Success Looks Like



After you’ve been with us for a while, success should mean:



I can concentrate on sales and growing Northwest Floors without worrying that something operational has been forgotten.



Customers receive updates without chasing us.



Fitters know where they’re going and what they’re doing.



Materials are ordered and arrive when required.



We know what stock we’re going to need next month.



Outstanding actions are followed up.



Our systems are organised.



Our calendar is organised.



Our customers receive great service.



And when something requires my attention, I receive the information I need to make a quick decision.



Eventually, I want to be able to take a holiday and know that the business continues operating without me constantly checking my phone.



⸻



Who Will Be Successful In This Role?



You’ll probably be a great fit if you are:



* Extremely organised

* Naturally proactive

* Curious

* Comfortable taking responsibility

* An excellent communicator

* Confident speaking and writing in English

* Comfortable speaking with UK customers

* Good at following things through

* Comfortable politely chasing people

* Able to prioritise

* Calm when things change

* Good at problem-solving

* Detail-focused

* Comfortable with technology

* Willing to learn

* Trustworthy

* Discreet

* Happy to admit when you don’t know something and then find the answer

* Interested in understanding the whole business rather than simply completing individual tasks



Experience as an Executive Assistant, Operations Assistant, Project Coordinator, Office Manager or similar role would be particularly useful.



Experience with CRM systems, QuickBooks, WhatsApp Business,
 management and calendar management would also be beneficial.



Previous flooring experience is not required.



A willingness to become knowledgeable about flooring is required.



⸻



Hours & Long-Term Opportunity



This will initially be approximately 20–25 hours per week.



Because our business, customers and fitting teams are based in the UK, you must be able to work with a meaningful overlap with UK business hours.



We can agree the exact working schedule with the successful candidate.



This is not intended to be a short-term freelance project.



I’m looking for somebody who wants to build a long-term working relationship with me and Northwest Floors.



For the right person, I expect the position, responsibility and hours to grow over time.



As my trust in you increases and your knowledge of the business develops, I want to progressively give you more autonomy.



⸻



About Me



I’m the owner of Northwest Floors and I’m entrepreneurial by nature.



I move quickly, have lots of ideas and often have several things happening simultaneously.



You may sometimes receive a three-minute voice note from me containing six completely unrelated things.



I need somebody who can take that information and turn it into organised actions.



I don’t expect perfection.



I don’t expect you to know everything.



I do expect honesty, initiative, communication and ownership.



If you make a mistake, tell me.



We’ll fix it, learn from it and improve the system so it’s less likely to happen again.



I’m looking for somebody who can eventually become a genuine right-hand person within the business.



⸻



How To Apply



Please do not send a generic copy-and-paste VA application.



I’m much more interested in how you think and communicate than receiving the perfect CV.



Start your application with the words:



OWN THE OUTCOME



This lets me know you’ve actually read the job description.



Then answer the following:



1. Tell me about a previous position where you supported a business owner or manager and had to manage lots of moving parts.



2. Give me a real example of something you noticed and dealt with without waiting for somebody to ask you.



3. One of our flooring fitters is due at a customer’s home tomorrow morning. At 3pm today, you discover the flooring hasn’t arrived and the fitter isn’t answering their phone. The customer currently believes everything is going ahead normally.



What would you do?



4. I send you a three-minute voice note containing six unrelated tasks. Explain exactly what you would do with it.



5. A customer asks you a flooring question and you don’t know the answer. What do you do?



6. Part of this position involves spending at least one paid hour every week learning about flooring. How would you approach learning an industry you currently know very little about?



7. You look at our schedule and notice we have several large LVT installations coming up next month. What would you check or do without waiting for me to ask?



8. What hours are you available to work in UK time?



9. What hourly or monthly salary are you looking for?



10. Please send me a short voice recording introducing yourself, telling me a little about yourself and explaining why you think you would be a good fit for this position.



I’m looking for someone who wants more than a list of tasks.



I’m looking for someone who wants to understand the business, take ownership and become an important part of where we’re going.



If that sounds like you, I’d love to hear from you.

title: Video Editor – Fitness Apparel Brand (Short-Form Content & Ads)
description:
SOUL OMEN is a growing men’s fitness apparel brand built around bodybuilding, discipline, suffering, growth, and embracing change.



We are looking for a skilled video editor to join our team and help us produce high-quality short-form content for Instagram, TikTok, and paid advertising.



Currently looking for part-time with the availability of fulltime, as we are growing quick and the job can very quickly scale into a full-time gig.



This is not a basic "cut clips and add captions" editing position. We want someone with a strong understanding of modern short-form content, pacing, storytelling, hooks, and performance-driven editing.



What You'll Do

Edit short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and Meta ads

Colorgrade raw SLOG footage

Edit UGC, athlete content, founder content, gym/lifestyle footage, and professional camera footage

Turn raw footage into engaging videos with strong hooks and pacing

Create multiple variations of successful concepts for testing

Edit both organic content and direct-response advertising creatives

Add captions, sound design, music, effects, transitions, zooms, B-roll, and other elements when appropriate

Repurpose longer footage into multiple short-form videos

Follow creative direction while also bringing your own ideas to improve the edit

Organize and manage raw footage and project files efficiently

Make revisions quickly based on feedback and performance data

title: Launch Budget Coordinator, STR Property Launches (Reconciliation Heavy, US Hours)
description:
LAUNCH BUDGET COORDINATOR, SHORT-TERM RENTAL PROPERTY LAUNCHES

Remote. US business hours.



PLEASE READ THIS WHOLE POST BEFORE APPLYING. There are instructions at the bottom, and how you follow them is the first thing we look at.



ABOUT US



We run full-service, hands-off management for short-term rental owners across the US. Part of that is launching a property: an owner hands us an empty house and we furnish it, wire it, stock it, style it, photograph it and open it to guests. The owner pays one all-in launch budget for that. Furniture, tech, accessories, and the services that install them.



This seat owns the record of every dollar in that budget. It is reconciliation work: vendor invoices against what we committed to, card charges against the plan, receipts filed the day they exist, spreadsheets that have to tie. We automate everything software can do. What software cannot do is notice that a vendor invoice and a card statement disagree by $16.48, d
 that the $16.48 matters, and go find out why. Right now that work sits with our founder, and that is the whole reason this seat exists.



We are growing, this is the first seat of its kind here, and it will not be the last one.



WHAT THIS ROLE REALLY IS



Every case below is real. The amounts are changed, for the same reason we explain further down.



Nineteen furniture lines on a live property are flagged as ordered. There is no order number behind any of them, no charge on any card, and no confirmation from the vendor.



Either they were bought and nobody wrote it down, or somebody typed a word into the wrong cell. The difference is $4,318.62. If you place that order and it was already placed, the owner pays for the same furniture twice, and nobody finds out for a month.



That is the job.



Here is more of it, in the same week.



- Two lines carry the same item name and two different product links, so the house is getting either four sofas or two, a $2,144.75 question, and the owner is reading it as one line.

- A vendor invoice hit the card as $9,340.55 on one day and another $812.07 a week later, because that vendor captures payment as items ship. The record held only the first number, so the property looked $812.07 cheaper than it was.

- A tax column on a delivery showed $22.50 per mattress and nothing on the other sixty items. That is not tax. It is a state recycling fee that is legitimately owed, and two people here have already gotten it wrong.

- A four-figure order shipped to one property's address and belonged to a different property's plan. The ship-to address is never the answer. The item list is.

- One plan column read $10,462.31 against an order total of $10,462.08. A twenty-three cent gap between two numbers computed from completely different inputs made the row look reconciled while the real figure underneath it sat $1,384.90 low.



Every one of those is solvable. None of them is solvable by someone who is willing to let it go.



So the honest description of this role: it is detective work on money. Most days it is a spreadsheet, a vendor invoice, a receipt and a browser. It is quiet and it is deliberate. The person who is great at it is the person who genuinely cannot leave a number alone when it does not tie, who would rather spend forty minutes finding the missing $16.48 than type over the cell and move on, and who gets a small amount of satisfaction when the last line finally closes at zero.



Your job in one sentence: keep the record true enough that the close-out number is right the first time. By the time that number goes to an owner there is very little left for anyone to check, because you kept the record true for the three months leading up to it. We read it before it goes anywhere, and it goes out over our name, not yours.



This is not task-based VA work. Nobody is going to send you a list each morning telling you which rows to price or which invoice to open. You run a weekly rhythm and you can read your own dashboard, so you already know.



If that reads as tedious to you, we would genuinely rather you skip this one. If it reads as a puzzle, keep going.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN



Your instrument is one Google Sheet per property, our launch budget tracker. It is the single record of what the property is buying, what it committed to, what actually got charged, and what is left. Every property in flight has one and you run all of them.



You grow into this in two phases. Phase one is keeping the record true on properties that are already running. Phase two is owning a property's budget from the day the tracker opens to the day it closes.



PHASE ONE, KEEPING THE RECORD TRUE



- Price every row on the plan that has no price. Find the item, confirm the variant, the size and the pack quantity, and put a real number on it.

- Load the Amazon and Wayfair carts against the plan. This is more mechanical than it sounds and it has real traps. Our Amazon cart holds a hard 50 lines, and line 51 silently pushes the oldest line out into Saved for later, so a 152 row accessories list is four separate orders and you d
 the batches up front. Re-adding an item that is already in the cart raises its quantity instead of warning you. You verify by item code and quantity, never by the badge in the corner.

- Tag every order back onto the plan rows it paid for, so nothing is bought that the sheet does not know about.

- Log every card charge as its own row, with the invoice's true order total rather than the first posting that showed up, and file the receipt the day it exists. A charge with no receipt cannot be cleanly billed back, which means a missing receipt is money the company cannot recover that month.

- Reconcile every vendor invoice against what we actually committed to, line by line, and produce the defect list. What was charged, what was ordered, what is missing, what does not agree, and which of those is a real problem versus a coi
.

- Run the flag pass every Friday. Filter the exception column and clear everything that is not clean. Some of our checks run from scripts on our side and we run them against your sheet, so your pass has to be clean before it reaches them.

- Chase our designer for the receipts, the property attributions and the open answers that nobody else is going to chase. The buying happens in person, in other states, on a company card, and store receipts print department codes instead of product names, so only the person who was standing there can say which room a $340 receipt belongs to. Nobody else will chase that, and after you start, nobody else has to. This is the one genuinely persistent, human thread in the job and it is a large part of its value.



PHASE TWO, OWNING THE BUDGET END TO END



- Open a tracker for a new property from our template and type the house into the quantity calculator: bedrooms, beds by size, baths, sleeps, TVs, floors. Half the quantities in the plan calculate themselves off those numbers, so this is not data entry, it is the foundation. Every count comes from a written source, and when two written sources disagree you flag it instead of picking a winner.

- Take the designer's spec in when it changes and surface what it moved: what got more expensive, what got cheaper, and which rows quietly disappeared. Never hand-merge two lists.

- Watch the envelope. The plan has a cap, and the week you first see that the plan is going to cross it, you say so out loud. Weeks early, not at the end. Warning early is the entire point of the number.

- Compute what owner money may be sent to pay down the company card, name the specific charges it covers, and evidence every one with a receipt. Then record the settlement against every row it paid. A row you forget to mark as settled asks for the same money again next month.

- Produce the close-out: the reconciliation that says whether the owner is owed a refund or owes a true-up, and the drafted invoice or refund figure behind it.



HELPING BUILD THE SYSTEM



- We have a written playbook for this seat and we are still finishing the SOPs behind it. You will help write them, in your own words, out of the work you actually did.

- Write down why a sheet looks the way it does, so the next person does not have to re-derive it. As we add properties this becomes more than one seat, and the person who runs it well is the person who trains the next one.



WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION IN THIS POST



You own the record. You never own the movement.



Nothing you do debits a bank, releases a wire, pays a card, or reaches an owner's inbox. Not once, not in an emergency, not on a deadline.



- You never fire a charge. Every single payment, card or eCheck or wire, is approved personally by our founder, on that specific charge, every time. There is no batch approval and there is no standing permission.

- You never move money out of any bank or merchant account. You compute what should be paid and you evidence it. He releases it.

- You do not place the orders. You build the cart, you verify it line by line, you hand it over with the batch, the total, the shipping address and the property reference it needs, and somebody else presses the button.

- You are not the property owner's contact. Not the approval schedule, not an invoice, not a refund figure, not an
 with a number in it. You draft. We send. Always.

- You never add, edit or verify a vendor's bank details or payee information. Nobody in this seat does. That is the wall against invoice fraud, and urgency is the exact pretext it exists to defeat.

- You have no banking, no payment gateway and no accounting system access, on purpose. If you ever find that you somehow can reach one, you do not act, you report it.



Read that as protection, not as distrust. The seat that keeps the record of the money is deliberately not the seat that moves it, because a record that can move money is not a record, it is an opinion. That separation is what makes your close-out number worth something, and it means that when money goes somewhere it should not have, it is structurally impossible for it to have been you. Very few jobs this close to real dollars give you that. We designed it that way on purpose, we will not ask you to bend it, and we think it is one of the best parts of the offer.



A WORD ABOUT CONFIDENTIALITY



You will see what we pay for goods and what the owner is billed for them. That information does not leave the company, ever, for any reason, including to an owner who asks you directly and including when they are being nice about it. If that is not a line you can hold comfortably, please do not apply. It is written into the agreement and we take it seriously.



The same applies in the other direction. You never structure anything: no splitting an order, sequencing a purchase, or shaping a number so it sits under a threshold. And no order, vendor or reimbursement that benefits you or anyone connected to you. Either one is immediate cause, even if the underlying purchase was perfectly fine. We say it out loud so nobody is surprised by it later.



MUST-HAVES



We are not going to write detail oriented here, because everybody says it about themselves and it predicts nothing. Here is what actually predicts success in this seat.



- 2+ years in a role where reconciling one document against another was the actual job. Accounts payable, bookkeeping, procurement, ecommerce operations, inventory control, order desk, audit support. Something where a number had to tie and you were the one who made it tie.

- You know that a total matching is not proof it is right. Two numbers built from completely different inputs can land within a dollar of each other by coi
, look tied, and hide a four-figure error underneath. Somebody who checks totals and stops will not survive here.

- You understand that one number can arrive as several charges. A single vendor order can hit a card as three postings weeks apart. Log the first one and the record is quietly wrong forever, and nothing on the sheet will tell you.

- You chase small discrepancies to the bottom. If a total is off by $16.48, we need the person who finds the $16.48, not the person who adjusts the total. You are also the person who can chase it, find that it is a legitimate fee and not an error, and say so, instead of forcing it to tie.

- You can hold an open discrepancy without doing either wrong thing with it. The two failure modes are dropping it because it is small and inventing a reason for it because you want it closed. Both are worse than a note that says unexplained, $16.48, chasing. If you have ever kept a variance open for two weeks because you refused to guess, tell us about it.

- You leave alone what you do not understand. Some of our sheets carry hand-marked rows whose meaning was never written down. Our standing rule is preserve, never interpret. A near-pattern is a trap, not a shortcut, and finishing one makes six edits nobody can undo. If your instinct is to tidy first and ask later, this seat will hurt.

- Real spreadsheet fluency, not proficient in Excel on a resume. SUMIFS, lookups, filters, spotting a hardcoded number sitting where a formula should be, and knowing what happens to a sheet when someone inserts a column into the middle of it. You will inherit sheets you did not build. We will test this and it is not a hard test if this is true of you. You do not need to code.

- You can tell someone senior to you that a number is wrong. Comfortably, in writing, with the evidence attached, and without softening it into something they can miss.

- You follow up politely and repeatedly with somebody who is busy and is not your subordinate. The designer chase is real and it does not resolve itself.

- Stamina for a long pass. Some days are 150 rows of the same check. We need the 150th to get the same attention as the first.

- Honest. If you have not confirmed something, you say so. You never report a status you did not verify and you never invent a number, a price, a quantity, a receipt or which property a charge belongs to. I do not know yet, here is how I am finding out, is always the right answer. This is the single most important item on this list and it is a hard gate at every stage of our process.

- Clear, professional written English. You will write to a US designer and to US vendor support about money, and you will write notes somebody reads six months later to understand why a row looks the way it does.

- Stable power and internet, plus a backup for outages.

- Able to work the fixed shift below. Please read the hours section carefully before you apply.



NICE-TO-HAVES



- Amazon Business, Wayfair Professional, or any trade, wholesale or B2B purchasing account.

- You have reconciled a credit card statement against a set of vendor invoices and found something.

- You have chased a vendor for a credit and won.

- Bookkeeping exposure, QuickBooks or Xero or similar, even read-only. You will not have a QuickBooks seat, but knowing what a reimbursement invoice has to say is useful.

- Furniture, interior design, hospitality FF and E, or construction procurement background.

- Short-term rental or property management background.

- You have built a tracker or a process that somebody else then used without you in the room.

- A little Google Apps Script or Python, or genuine curiosity about the scripts behind our sheets. Not required. Rewarded.



HOURS AND TIMEZONE



This is a fixed US business-hours shift. Please read this section before you d
 anything else about the job.



- 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Pacific, Monday through Friday. Eight hours a day, 40 hours a week.

- In the Philippines that is 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM the following day. Midnight to eight in the morning. That is an overnight shift and we are not going to describe it as anything else.

- The shift moves by one hour when the US changes to and from daylight saving time. Nothing else changes.

- The work itself is asynchronous in nature. Spreadsheets, invoices, receipts, carts, reconciliation. Almost none of it needs somebody else awake at the same moment, and you are not on a phone all day. The genuinely synchronous part is small: the designer, and occasionally a vendor's support line. Both of those sit inside the shift.

- Our other US-facing seats run a ten hour US day. This one is eight.

- You are online and responsive for the whole shift, not signed in with notifications off.

- Some deadlines in this job are actual dates. The Friday flag pass happens on Friday. Ordering deadlines ahead of a launch are the other kind, and they do not move.

- No weekends. Nothing lands on you outside the shift. Emergencies stay with us.



Be honest with yourself about that before you apply. If midnight to 8:00 AM does not fit your life, please do not apply, and there is no hard feeling in that.



If you are somewhere other than the Philippines, do the conversion yourself and tell us on the form what 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific is where you are. We do read that answer.



COMPENSATION



- $750 per month, for the arrangement above.

- The rate is flat. Phase two pays the same as phase one. We would rather say that plainly than describe a step-up we have not committed to, so you can plan on this number.

- Merit review at 90 days after conversion, then annually. That is where the rate gets revisited.

- We honor 13th month pay. We offer flexible coordinated time off and we cover your equipment. We treat our people well and the good ones grow with us.

- Paid trial first. Before any ongoing offer there is a short paid project, a couple of hours of real work, and we pay you for it.

- The first four weeks are an Initial Evaluation Term at close to full rate, so both sides get a real look before anyone commits.



HOW WE HIRE



We use a multi-step process and it is deliberately demanding. Every stage is something you do on your own time, and we do not schedule a single call until you have already shown us how you work.



In order: a short application form, a 2-minute video, a written reconciliation exercise, a personality assessment, then an interview and a paid trial. Budget roughly two to three hours of your own time across all of it before the paid trial, which we pay for. The personality assessment is a tiebreaker, not a gate, and nobody is rejected on it alone.



Each step starts when you finish the one before it. There is no cohort and there is no closing date. The video request reaches you within a minute of your form landing, and you get 48 hours from that
. Clear it and the reconciliation exercise comes to you, with 72 hours from that
. Clear that and the assessment comes, with 24 hours. Every clock runs from your own
, not from a date on a calendar, so applying today and applying in a month get you exactly the same runway.



This posting stays up until somebody accepts an offer. Then it comes down and the form closes.



The reconciliation exercise is the stage that d
 this seat. It is a real invoice against a real plan with the names taken out, it does not tie, and the reason it does not tie is not the reason you will first think it is. There is no trick, but there is a wrong answer that most people give, and it is the confident one.



Deadlines are real at every stage, and they are personal to you rather than to a calendar. If you miss one, you are out. Please do not ask for an extension.



HOW TO APPLY



Fill out the form linked at the very bottom of this post.



Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. Please do not message us on this platform, do not
 us, and do not send a resume in a reply. Only form submissions are looked at. We know that is strict. It is the first filter and it is working as intended.



Read the form carefully. One of the questions is there to check that you read this post.

title: Executive Virtual Assistant
description:
$5–$7 USD/hour | Long-Term Position | Growth Opportunity



We are looking for a smart, dependable, highly organized Virtual Assistant who wants to become a long-term part of our team.



We are not looking for someone who simply completes assigned tasks and waits for the next instruction. We want someone who takes ownership, follows through, thinks ahead, brings ideas, and helps us improve the way we operate.



You do not need to know everything when you start. We will train the right person. What matters most is that you are intelligent, resourceful, dependable, comfortable with technology, and able to learn independently.



Prior appraisal experience is NOT required. We can teach you the appraisal-related portion of the position.



Responsibilities



You will assist with:



Typing and preparing appraisal-related reports and documents

Answering incoming business calls

Communicating professionally with homeowners, lenders, attorneys, real estate professionals, and other clients

Scheduling appraisal appointments

Responding to appraisal bid requests

Negotiating fees and turn times within company guidelines

Managing
s, calendars, orders, files, and client follow-ups

Keeping track of outstanding items and following up without needing to be reminded

Helping organize and improve company systems and workflows

Using ChatGPT and other technology to improve productivity

Assisting with website, marketing, advertising, and business improvement projects as needed



Again, appraisal experience is not required. We are willing to train someone who demonstrates strong learning ability, attention to detail, initiative, professionalism, and reliability.



Schedule & Availability



This position requires consistent availability during U.S. Central Time (CT) business hours.



Work schedules will generally fall within one of the following shifts:



8:00 AM – 5:00 PM CT

9:00 AM – 6:00 PM CT

10:00 AM – 7:00 PM CT



The specific schedule will be determined based on company needs and discussed during the hiring process.



Because this position includes answering business calls, communicating with clients, scheduling appointments, and handling time-sensitive matters, applicants must be able to reliably and consistently work their assigned Central Time schedule.



Computer & Workstation Requirements



Because this position involves working with multiple programs, documents, websites,
s, appraisal software, and other systems at the same time, you must already have an appropriate workstation.



You must have:



A reliable computer capable of handling your daily workload

At least two computer monitors/screens that can be used together as one workstation

Reliable high-speed internet

A working microphone and audio setup for calls and meetings

A dependable backup plan for internet or power outages



A desktop computer plus a completely separate laptop that cannot function as a second connected display does NOT meet the two-screen requirement.



You must be able to work across at least two screens simultaneously from the same workstation.



Please do not apply if you do not currently meet this requirement.



We Want Someone Who Contributes



We do not want someone who does something a certain way simply because “that’s how it has always been done.”



If you notice a better, faster, more organized, or more efficient way to do something, we want you to tell us.



We want someone who:



Takes ownership of assignments from beginning to completion

Follows up without being asked

Notices when something still needs attention

Thinks ahead

Identifies problems and suggests solutions

Brings new ideas to the company

Researches better ways of doing things

Is comfortable respectfully recommending changes

Wants to help the company grow, not simply complete tasks



If you are given responsibility for something, we should not have to continuously remind you that it still needs to be completed.

AI & Technology



You do not need to be an AI expert.



However, you must be comfortable learning new technology and figuring things out independently.



We may ask you to research ChatGPT, AI tools, automation, websites, marketing systems, software, or other technology that could help our business.

If you are carefully reading this job posting, use the exact subject line “Michael Jackson Is Dancing” when submitting your application.



You Should Be

Reliable and consistent

Strong in written and spoken English

Comfortable speaking with U.S.-based clients by phone

Professional and confident

Appraisal experience is a plus but is NOT required.



Pay & Growth



Starting pay is $5–$7 USD/hour, depending on experience and demonstrated ability.



We plan to conduct a performance review after approximately 90 days. Strong performance, increased independence, and greater responsibility can lead to increased compensation and advancement.



We are looking for someone who wants to become an important part of the company over the long term.



How to Apply

Describe your experience answering phones and communicating with clients.

Why are you interested in a long-term position?

Voice Recording Required

This position requires regular communication with U.S.-based clients by phone, so the voice recording will help us evaluate spoken English, communication style, professionalism, clarity, and comfort speaking.

Interview Process & Typing Test

 to move forward with you, we will provide a typing test that must be completed as part of the interview process.

s, documents, reports, and computer-based work, typing ability will be considered when evaluating candidates.



Professional References

Name

Company

Your working relationship

 address

Important:

title: Process Specialist
description:

-Proven ability to write and update SOPs for both technical and non-technical audiences.

-Experience using Trainual or similar documentation, knowledge management, or LMS platforms.

-Experience with Trainual or similar documentation/training platforms is highly preferred.

-Construction, electrical, facilities, or field-operations experience is a plus.

-Experience supporting training, onboarding, or internal enablement initiatives is a plus.



Equipment Requirements:

Benefits:

-Growth opportunities in a well-established company.

-Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.

-Opportunity for advancement within the company.

-A supportive and collaborative work environment.

-Company-observed paid United States holidays (full time).

How to Apply:

If you are ready to join Power Plus Systems, LLC, a well-established residential electrical contractor that values its team members and offers excellent benefits, please submit your application through the link below.




/internationalform



Power Plus Systems, LLC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Join us at Power Plus Systems, LLC, and be part of our continued success as we embark on the next 20 years of excellence in residential electrical contracting!

title: Experienced Appointment Setter / DM Closer
description:
100K Solutions is looking for an **experienced Appointment Setter / DM Closer** to join our team long-term.



We need someone who can take ownership of our inbound leads and DMs, communicate professionally, qualify prospects, follow up consistently, handle basic objections, and turn conversations into **qualified booked appointments**.



This is not a basic VA position where you simply copy and paste scripts. You need to understand sales conversations, know how to build rapport, recognize buying signals, and move prospects toward the next step without sounding robotic or overly aggressive.



### Responsibilities



- Respond to new inbound leads and DMs quickly.

- Communicate with prospects through social media, SMS, and our CRM.

- Qualify leads based on their goals, current situation, urgency, and ability to invest.

- Turn qualified conversations into booked appointments.

- Follow up consistently with leads who do not respond or are not ready immediately.

- Re-engage older leads already in our pipeline.

- Handle common objections around price, timing, trust, and readiness.

- Confirm appointments and help reduce no-shows.

- Keep accurate notes and update every lead's status inside the CRM.

- Make sure no qualified lead falls through the cracks.

- Follow our scripts and sales process while still communicating naturally.

- Provide daily updates on conversations, follow-ups, appointments booked, and lead status.

- Communicate important lead information to our closer and management team.



### Requirements



- Previous experience as an **appointment setter, DM setter, sales VA, or DM closer is required**.

- Strong written English and communication skills.

- Experience handling inbound leads and sales conversations.

- Comfortable qualifying prospects and asking sales-related questions.

- Experience handling objections and following up with prospects.

- Ability to communicate naturally instead of relying completely on copy-and-paste responses.

- Strong organization and attention to detail.

- Experience using a CRM is preferred.

- Ability to follow systems, scripts, and instructions.

- Must be reliable and available during agreed working hours.

- Must be able to work independently without constant reminders or supervision.

- Must be coachable and willing to improve based on feedback.



### What We're Looking For



We want someone who understands that **following up is just as important as responding to new leads**.

OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

---

The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.
